collins.hedgehog: Become best in the world at running consumer-electronics superstores (wide selection, service, low prices, satisfaction) and rolling the model out on a national scale with disciplined systems. Collins gives the economic denominator as profit per geographic region rather than per store, reflecting regional economies of scale in distribution, advertising and management.
hedgehog_key_points: profit per region (regional economies of scale)
collins.stop_doing: Stop running a patchwork of formats (leased departments in discount chains, small audio stores, mail-order, scattered acquired chains) and commit capital to the superstore model.
stop_doing_key_points: exit leased departments and scattered small formats
concentrate resources on the superstore model
collins.leader_type: Level 5 (Alan Wurtzel: the founder's son, a lawyer, modest and questioning; he led by asking hard questions instead of announcing answers, built a strong team, and set up his successor to succeed).
brutal_facts: the 1974 loss showed the leased-department and mixed-format model was not working
the superstore format required a large capital bet relative to the company's size
acquired chains such as Lafayette in New York were struggling

later_history: Renamed Circuit City Stores in 1984 under Richard Sharp. It passed $1B in sales by 1987 and $2B by 1990. Collins reports cumulative returns about 18.5x the market for 1982-1997, the highest in the study. Lafayette was closed in 1986. CarMax was launched in 1993. Circuit City lost ground to Best Buy from the mid-1990s; the DIVX venture failed (about $233M) and appliances were dropped in 2000. It eliminated commissioned sales in 2003, and in 2007 laid off about 3,400 better-paid store staff. It filed for Chapter 11 in November 2008 and announced liquidation in January 2009; all stores closed by March 2009. It is a How the Mighty Fall case.
notes: Track A matched pair with A06 (Silo). greatness_label = 1 because the company stayed great for 15+ years after 1982, despite the later collapse. Sources disagree on the first superstore date: Wikipedia gives May 1975 for the Loading Dock, while FundingUniverse gives 1974. The dossier avoids an exact year. Collins's denominator is confirmed by a secondary summary; other hedgehog wording is paraphrased from memory of Ch. 5.
